correctness.rationale: The skew-polynomial PBW rule yields the displayed commutator matrix after division by the nonzero zeta-1; the only outputs are xy, x²y, xy² and x²y². For a nonzero linear part, the first row, the independent degree-two restrictions in the middle rows, and the nonzero degree-three restriction in the last row give rank four. With zero linear part, the middle block has determinant zeta ce-d². If (c,e) is nonzero the last row adds one to its rank; if c=e=0 and d is nonzero the last row adds nothing to rank two. The zero quadratic part gives rank one precisely when the degree-three part is nonzero. The cone has (q-1)²+(2q-1)=q² points, so the rank-two triples count as q²-1 on the cone plus q-1 off it, and the rank-three triples number (q-1)(q²-1). Free coefficients then give the full table, valid also in characteristic two since the root identities and the independence arguments do not divide by 2. Commuting in 1+J is equivalent to commuting in J; scalars do not affect ranks, and an element of rank r has class size q^r. Dividing the element counts by q^(r+1) and summing reproduces k=q^4+2q³-2q and the stated probability. The frozen verification documents and output cover slices over F_4, F_7 and F_13, not full enumeration of all q^9 elements; the uploaded checker was not executed.

value.rationale: The exact adjoint spectrum is a natural invariant of this local algebra and determines the complete class-size distribution in its algebra group. The quadratic cone and the off-cone pure-xy exceptions give the nontrivial middle ranks; neither a generic-rank computation nor the available left-multiplication invariant determines their multiplicities. The result gives a characteristic-uniform exact census at the primitive cubic twist, useful as the baseline against which the separate order-four rank disappearance is visible. Value lies in the whole census, not in the routine summation or class-size conversion by themselves.
